TraceContract.purpose: Define the cross-module observability identifiers and the BLOCK_* marker grammar that lets verification scenarios assert both outcome correctness and trajectory correctness from captured stderr/log output. Schema is decoupled from runtime: every M-XXX module ships eprintln! markers conforming to this grammar today, and a future tracing-layer crate (Phase-B1) will harvest them into structured events without changing the on-the-wire format consumed by tests.

trace_id.semantics: One per process invocation. Time-ordered so trace archives sort naturally. Survives until process exit.
trace_id.emission: Appended automatically by Phase-B1 tracing layer; not present in eprintln! markers today.

req_id.semantics: One per renderer→main IPC roundtrip. Renderer generates; main echoes back unchanged in both ack and event fanout payloads.
req_id.emission: Phase-B3 (M-013-A/M-013-B IPC bridge); not present today (no IPC layer yet).

session_chain_id.semantics: Identifies a window+renderer session. Survives in- process IPC chain; resets per new window. Used to correlate renderer-side console with main-side events.
session_chain_id.emission: Phase-B3 (M-001 window lifecycle hooks); not present today.

conventions.c: First segment of the Rust module path, lowercase, snake_case as already in source. Examples: legacy, dialog, migration_strings, mt_paths, cancel_log, main. NOT the M-XXX ID — markers stay grep-friendly without cross-referencing the module catalog.
Function name OR a named logical block within a function (chosen when one function emits multiple distinct milestones). Snake-case.

SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE noun describing the milestone. Names are unique across the codebase — never repeat a BLOCK_NAME in different modules even if their domains differ; use suffixes (e.g. BLOCK_LEGACY_FOUND, BLOCK_DIALOG_OPEN) instead.

SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE noun describing an error/abort/coercion. The `MT_` prefix is reserved for non-milestone identifiers that cross module boundaries — typically defined as a `pub const` in the producing module (e.g. MT_PREFS_V1_RUNNING in prefs.rs) and embedded in the call site's emit marker. Distinct namespace from BLOCK_*; tests assert against the exact byte string for stability.
Optional inline structured fields. Stable key names; values quoted only when whitespace is present. Avoid logging anything matching token regexes or path-leaking PII.

edge-cases.ec: Symlink loop A→B→A: readlink chain bounded; returns MT_FS_SYMLINK_LOOP after N=40 hops (matches POSIX ELOOP).
Broken symlink (target deleted): stat returns MT_FS_BROKEN_LINK; read does NOT fall back to creating target.
Symlink pointing outside sandbox root: canonicalize then re-validate against M-010; rejected BEFORE open(2).
Non-regular inode (FIFO, socket, block/char device, /dev/zero): S_ISREG check fails → MT_FS_NOT_REGULAR. Must not block on read from FIFO.
Filename containing NUL byte (`foo\0bar`) or path separator inside segment: rejected at BLOCK_VALIDATE_PATH (pre-CString conversion).
Windows reserved names (CON, PRN, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) with or without extension: rejected on Windows target only; allowed on Unix.
Trailing whitespace / trailing dot filenames on Windows: rejected (NTFS silently strips, causing write-vs-read path mismatch).
Disk-full mid-write: write(2) returns ENOSPC → atomic temp+rename contract ensures original file untouched; temp cleaned up.
fsync ordering: write-to-temp → fsync(temp) → rename → fsync(parent-dir). All four syscalls observable via strace/dtruss.
Read-only parent directory: creating new file returns EACCES → MT_FS_PERM_DENIED; no partial file left.
macOS TCC denial (Desktop/Documents/Downloads without entitlement): errno 1 EPERM → stable MT_FS_TCC_DENIED distinct from MT_FS_PERM_DENIED.
External mv/rm between validate_path and open: open returns ENOENT → MT_FS_RACE_VANISHED (not MT_FS_NOT_FOUND) so UI can refresh.

negative-assertions.no: No BLOCK_READ_FROM_DISK emitted for NUL-byte path, FIFO, reserved name, or post-canonicalize out-of-sandbox path.
On ENOSPC during write, original file SHA256 unchanged after error; exactly one BLOCK_ATOMIC_RENAME failure log.
Symlink loop emits exactly one BLOCK_RESOLVE_SYMLINK with hops==40 then error — not 40 separate logs.

edge-cases.ec: UTF-8 truncated at chunk boundary mid-codepoint (`\xE2\x98` of `\xE2\x98\x83` ☃): detector must defer decision or buffer tail — never misclassify as Latin-1.
Overlong UTF-8 (`\xC0\x80` for NUL): rejected as invalid UTF-8, does NOT roundtrip.
Unpaired UTF-16 surrogate (`\xD8\x00` LE without low surrogate): flagged MT_ENC_INVALID_SURROGATE; not silently replaced with U+FFFD in strict mode.
BOM masquerade: UTF-16LE BOM (`\xFF\xFE`) prefix on otherwise UTF-8 bytes: BOM wins, decoded as UTF-16LE; emits BLOCK_DETECT_BOM with bom="utf-16le".
0-byte file: returns default encoding (UTF-8) with BOM=none, newline=LF; no chardet call.
1-byte file (`A`): chardet low-confidence → fallback UTF-8 deterministically (not random).
File containing only BOM (3 bytes EF BB BF): treated as UTF-8 empty; write-back preserves BOM if user didn't toggle.
Latin-1 vs Windows-1252 vs MacRoman vs ISO-8859-15: bytes `\x80\x99\xA4` decode differently; fixture per codec; chardet confidence + tiebreak rule logged at BLOCK_CHARDET_GUESS.
CP932 vs CP936 vs CP949: same high-byte pair decodes to Japanese/Chinese/Korean; assertion pins detector output per fixture (not "any of three").
Mixed encoding (first 1KB UTF-8 + second 1KB Shift-JIS): detector returns majority or MT_ENC_MIXED; decoder either fails fast or produces U+FFFD with marker BLOCK_DECODE_REPLACEMENT { count }.
CRLF detection with CR byte mid-UTF-16 codepoint (`\x0D\x00` = U+000D, not a line break): newline detector runs on DECODED text, not raw bytes.
File content in NFC vs NFD: byte-roundtrip preserves original form (no silent NFC re-normalization). SHA256 in == SHA256 out when no edit.

V-M-031.module-surface: Renderer: src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/diffView.vue — new Vue SFC wrapping CodeMirror 5 MergeView addon. Pattern follows existing src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/sourceCode.vue (shared editor chrome, lifecycle hooks, theme wiring). MergeView instantiated with `origLeft` (baseline) and `value` (current content), using diff-match-patch as the diff algorithm provider. Supports inline (combined pane, default) and side-by-side (two-pane, toggle via toolbar button) modes with synchronized scrolling. Renderer: src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/index.vue — extended with third editor mode 'diff' alongside 'wysiwyg' and 'sourceCode'. Cmd+D keyboard shortcut toggles diff mode on/off. When entering diff mode, current content captured and baseline fetched via Tauri invoke `mt_diff_baseline`. When exiting, previous mode (wysiwyg or sourceCode) restored. diffView component conditionally mounted via v-if alongside existing editor components. Renderer: src/renderer/src/store/editor.js — per-tab state extended with `diffMode: boolean`, `diffBaseline: string|null`, `diffBaselineSource: 'file'|'git'|null` fields. Tab state persisted across tab switches. Backend: src-tauri/src/m031_diff.rs — new Tauri command `mt_diff_baseline` accepting file path, returning `{ baseline: String, source: "file"|"git" }`. Resolution order: (1) check for `{path}.before` sibling file, (2) if in git repo, attempt `git show HEAD:{relative_path}`, (3) return error with reason. All paths validated through SecurityCtx sandbox. Git invocation uses `std::process::Command` with timeout. Backend: src-tauri/src/main.rs — register `mt_diff_baseline` in Builder invoke_handler chain. Dependencies: `diff-match-patch` npm package (new, ~8KB gzip); `codemirror/addon/merge/merge.js` (already installed, ~38KB); `codemirror/addon/merge/merge.css` (already installed). Auto-detect: when a file is opened and a `.before` sibling exists, diff mode is automatically suggested/activated (configurable via preference `autoDiffOnBeforeFile`, default true).

race-conditions.R3: tab-switch-during-baseline-fetch — user presses Cmd+D on tab A, then immediately switches to tab B before baseline returns; invoke response arrives for tab A while tab B is active; response stored in tab A's editor store state; when user switches back to tab A, diff view renders from stored baseline; no orphan render on wrong tab; BLOCK_BASELINE_STORED_DEFERRED tab=A.

race-conditions.R5: before-file-deleted-while-diff-open — .before file existed at diff-enter time but is deleted externally while diff view is open; watcher fires; diff view shows stale baseline (acceptable — baseline is a snapshot); banner appears "Baseline file removed — diff shows last loaded baseline"; BLOCK_BASELINE_SOURCE_REMOVED.
race-conditions.R6: concurrent-baseline-requests — multiple tabs opened simultaneously with .before files (e.g., session restore); each invokes mt_diff_baseline independently; Rust handler is stateless per-call; no shared mutable state; concurrent execution safe; BLOCK_BASELINE_LOADED carries tab_id for correlation.

V-M-032.texture-audit:
CRITICAL FINDING: loadChange(change) at editor.js:116 expects change.data with { markdown, filename, encoding, lineEnding, ... } but APPLY_FILE_CHANGE at editor.js:1339 is called from project.js:232 with only { pathname } — change.data is undefined. This is a LATENT BUG: the reload-on-external-change path crashes on destructuring undefined. Never triggered because autoSave defaults to false and the notification action path (line 1381) hits the same crash.
Existing infrastructure: - Watcher: m013b/watch.rs emits on "mt::watch::event" channel (not "mt::file-changed"). WatchEvent shape: { subscriptionId, kind, paths[] }. Debounce: 200ms (DEBOUNCE_TICK). - Project store: project.js:192 _handleWatchEvent receives kind="modify" → calls editorStore.APPLY_FILE_CHANGE('change', { pathname }). - File read: ipcFs.read(path) → invoke('mt::fs::read', { path }) returns UTF-8 string. Available for frontend file reading. - Muya API: setMarkdown(markdown, cursor, isRenderCursor, muyaIndexCursor, blocks) at muya/lib/index.js:190. getCursor() at :186. NO getScrollTop/setScrollTop — scroll managed by editor.vue via DOM. - Tab state: isSaved flag (false = dirty). cursor, scrollTop, history preserved in tab object. - autoSave default: false (preferences.js:9). - loadChange at editor.js:116 creates fresh FileState via getSingleFileState, overwrites tab via Object.assign — cursor/scrollTop from NEW state (not preserved from old).
Scope revision: M-032 is NOT "add watcher + reload from scratch." It is: 1. FIX the broken loadChange path (add ipcFs.read before calling loadChange) 2. PRESERVE cursor/scrollTop across reload (save before Object.assign, restore after) 3. ADD auto-reload for non-dirty files regardless of autoSave preference (new "liveReload" pref, default true) 4. ADD same-content skip (hash compare before muya.setMarkdown) 5. ADD 100ms settle delay after debounced event to avoid reading mid-write
V-M-032.module-surface: Renderer: src/renderer/src/store/editor.js — (a) Fix APPLY_FILE_CHANGE 'change' branch: async read file via ipcFs.read(pathname) + construct data object with { markdown, filename, encoding, lineEnding, ... } BEFORE calling loadChange. This fixes the latent bug. (b) In loadChange: save old cursor + scrollTop BEFORE Object.assign(tab, newFileState). Restore after. (c) New preference "liveReload" (default: true). When liveReload=true AND isSaved=true: auto-reload without notification. When liveReload=false: fall back to existing notification behavior. (d) Same-content optimization: compare old markdown hash vs new before calling bus.emit('file-changed'). Skip if identical. (e) 100ms setTimeout after watcher event before reading file (settle delay for agent burst writes). Renderer: src/renderer/src/store/preferences.js — add liveReload: true default. Backend: NO changes needed. Watcher infrastructure (m013b/watch.rs) and ipcFs.read (m002_fs.rs) already exist.

mental-walkthroughs.walkthrough-1: 1. User opens file.md in Mark, edits some text, saves (isSaved=true) 2. Claude Code writes file.md via tool_use (file write) 3. notify-debouncer fires after 200ms quiet: WatchEvent { kind: "modify", paths: ["/path/file.md"] } 4. project.js._handleWatchEvent → editorStore.APPLY_FILE_CHANGE('change', { pathname }) 5. NEW: APPLY_FILE_CHANGE checks liveReload pref + isSaved flag 6. NEW: setTimeout(100ms) settle delay 7. NEW: await ipcFs.read(pathname) → markdown string 8. NEW: construct data = { markdown, filename: path.basename(pathname), encoding: tab.encoding, lineEnding: tab.lineEnding, ... } 9. NEW: hash compare: if markdown === tab.markdown → BLOCK_RELOAD_SKIPPED reason=no_diff, return 10. Save old cursor/scrollTop: const { cursor: oldCursor, scrollTop: oldScrollTop } = tab 11. loadChange({ pathname, data }) → Object.assign(tab, newFileState) 12. Restore: tab.cursor = oldCursor; tab.scrollTop = oldScrollTop 13. bus.emit('file-changed', { markdown, cursor: oldCursor, scrollTop: oldScrollTop, ... }) 14. editor.vue handleFileChange → muya.setMarkdown(markdown, oldCursor, ...) 15. editor.vue scrollToCords(oldScrollTop) RESULT: Editor shows new content, cursor stays at same position, scroll doesn't jump
mental-walkthroughs.walkthrough-2: 1. User types unsaved text (isSaved=false) 2. Claude Code writes file.md 3. Watcher fires → APPLY_FILE_CHANGE 4. Check: isSaved=false → dirty conflict 5. Show notification: "File changed on disk. Reload / Keep mine" 6a. User clicks "Reload": await ipcFs.read → loadChange → content replaced, unsaved edits lost (user chose this) 6b. User clicks "Keep mine": dismiss notification, mark tab.isSaved=false, keep current content RESULT: No silent data loss
mental-walkthroughs.walkthrough-3: 1. Claude Code writes file.md 5 times in 200ms (common with tool_use edit chains) 2. notify-debouncer coalesces all 5 events into ONE after 200ms quiet period 3. ONE WatchEvent { kind: "modify" } fires 4. 100ms settle delay 5. Read file → gets final content (5th write) 6. ONE reload in editor RESULT: No flicker, no 5x reload, correct final content
mental-walkthroughs.walkthrough-4: 1. User presses Cmd+S → file written to disk 2. Watcher detects OUR OWN write → fires WatchEvent modify 3. APPLY_FILE_CHANGE: settle delay 100ms → read file → content hash matches current tab.markdown 4. BLOCK_RELOAD_SKIPPED reason=no_diff RESULT: No unnecessary reload after save
mental-walkthroughs.walkthrough-5: 1. User opens file via Cmd+O (no project root, file opened standalone) 2. No watcher subscribed for this file (watcher is per-project-root in project.js) 3. External change → no event fires → no reload GAP: Live-reload only works for files inside an open project. Standalone files have no watcher. FUTURE: M-032 could add per-tab watcher subscription for standalone files. Scope decision for user.

failure-scenarios.F1: file-read-error — external write replaces file with unreadable permissions; ipcFs.read rejects; catch error; show toast "Could not reload: permission denied"; editor keeps old content; BLOCK_RELOAD_FAILED reason=io_error.
failure-scenarios.F2: invalid-utf8 — external tool writes binary/Latin-1 content; Rust mt::fs::read returns error (read_to_string fails on non-UTF8); catch; keep old content; toast error.
failure-scenarios.F3: watcher-stopped — notify-debouncer thread crashes or OS FSEvents limit reached; no events fire; user must manually re-open file; BLOCK_WATCHER_LOST logged when detected via watchdog (future enhancement).
failure-scenarios.F4: tab-closed-during-read — user closes tab while async ipcFs.read is in-flight; read completes; tab no longer in tabs array; loadChange returns early at line 132-143. No crash.

race-conditions.R1: user-types-during-read — user starts typing while async read is pending (100ms settle + read time); isSaved transitions to false during this window; read completes → re-check isSaved: if now false, show conflict notification instead of auto-replacing. GUARD: re-check dirty flag after read.
race-conditions.R2: tab-switch-during-read — user switches tab while read for tab A is pending; read completes; store updates tab A state (not visible); on switch back to A, handleFileChange fires from bus. No wrong-tab contamination.
race-conditions.R3: save-races-reload — user Cmd+S at same instant watcher fires; save writes file (updates mtime), then reload reads file; content from reload matches save content → hash skip → no duplicate work.
race-conditions.R4: two-files-changed-simultaneously — two watcher events for different files; two parallel async reads; each targets correct tab by pathname match. No cross-contamination.

numeric-thresholds.T1: Reload latency (watcher event → editor updated): ≤500ms for files under 100KB on M2 Mac. Breakdown: 200ms debounce + 100ms settle + ~50ms read + ~50ms muya parse. BLOCK_LIVE_RELOAD.elapsed_ms measured from watcher event timestamp.
numeric-thresholds.T2: Debounce: existing 200ms in m013b/watch.rs. Settle delay: 100ms added in APPLY_FILE_CHANGE. Total: 300ms from last write to read attempt.
numeric-thresholds.T3: Memory: reload of 1MB file adds ≤5MB transient heap (two copies of markdown string + muya block tree rebuild). Old blocks GC'd after render.
numeric-thresholds.T4: No main-thread block >50ms: ipcFs.read is async (IPC round-trip); muya.setMarkdown is synchronous but sub-50ms for <100KB files.

edge-cases.E1: Empty file — external tool truncates to 0 bytes; read returns ""; muya.setMarkdown("") → empty editor; no crash.
edge-cases.E2: Same content (touch) — content hash matches; skip reload. Hash: simple string equality (markdown strings are typically <1MB, equality is fast).
edge-cases.E3: Standalone file (no project) — file opened via Cmd+O without project root; no watcher subscription exists; external changes NOT detected. Known limitation. Future: per-tab watcher for standalone files.
edge-cases.E4: Very large file (>1MB) — read + muya.setMarkdown may take >50ms; consider requestIdleCallback for non-active tabs. Active tab: accept the jank for large files.
edge-cases.E5: File renamed externally — watcher fires "remove" + "create"; handled as unlink (banner) + potential re-open if new name matches. Complex edge case; defer to future.

log-markers.M4: [editor][reload][BLOCK_RELOAD_FAILED reason=io_error|parse_error path=... err=...] — read or parse failed

negative-assertions.N1: Reload NEVER silently discards unsaved user edits (isSaved=false MUST trigger conflict flow).
negative-assertions.N2: Reload NEVER fires for same-content writes (hash compare gate).
negative-assertions.N3: loadChange NEVER called with undefined change.data (the latent bug MUST be fixed).
negative-assertions.N4: Reload NEVER runs for files outside open project roots (watcher scope is per-project).
